description: Public edition: Integrates biological measurements into models of organ interactions, disease processes, and treatment responses.
body:
Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model. Integrates biological measurements into models of organ interactions, disease processes, and treatment responses.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 54 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Medicine, Biology, and Designed Life Systems". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Whole-cell models exist (Mycoplasma genitalium, Karr 2012); whole-organism human models are far off, with organ-level twins emerging.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Integrates biological measurements into models of organ interactions, disease processes, and treatment responses.
body:
Known science foundations of Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model.

Karr et al.'s 2012 whole-cell model of Mycoplasma genitalium integrated 28 submodels. The Physiome Project models organs. Cardiac and liver digital twins guide research. Human whole-body models remain coarse. Multi-scale integration from molecules to organs is the active frontier.

Key quantity check (Genes in Mycoplasma genitalium whole-cell model / genes in a human): computed ratio 0.02625 against the reference value, relative error 0.001901, within the stated tolerance of 0.2. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Integrates biological measurements into models of organ interactions, disease processes, and treatment responses.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model.

Human biology has ~37 trillion cells; full resolution is impossible. Parameter uncertainty dwarfs model precision. Validation needs data that does not exist yet.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 10.85 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is model genes (bacterial) vs human cells at 10.85 orders of magnitude (human cells larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

3. Multi-scale human models (coarse) (maturity 2/5, cost 3/5, risk 3/5; score -0.5).

description: Public edition: Integrates biological measurements into models of organ interactions, disease processes, and treatment responses.
body:
Unresolved problems for Whole-Organism Digital Physiology Model, in priority order (research burden index 30, 3 blocking):

Scaling to human complexity (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

Parameter identifiability (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Clinical validation (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

body:

Whole-cell model guides an experiment (weight 0.35; SATISFIED).

Human-scale model informs a trial (weight 0.25; not yet satisfied).

Tier: experimentally supported. Whole-cell models exist (Mycoplasma genitalium, Karr 2012); whole-organism human models are far off, with organ-level twins emerging.

Maturity projection (deterministic logistic model, current level 5/9, research intensity 0.6, 1 blockers): +5yr: maturity 6.04/9; +15yr: maturity 7.37/9; +30yr: maturity 8.34/9. This is a model, not a prediction - it shows what steady research effort would imply under stated assumptions.
